hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, stores, persons). Persons share the same business entity number, so person data attaches here as satellites rather than a separate hub. Email addresses and credentials are keyed by the same number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Countries and regions identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: States and provinces identified by their own number.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units in which people work. Keyed on the stable DepartmentID because department names can change.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts. Keyed on the stable ShiftID because shift names and definitions can be adjusted.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates whose applications are held by HR.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product master. ProductNumber is the business-recognised natural key (REQ-002), but every dependent relation (inventory, work orders, BOM, cost/price history, transactions, reviews, photos, documents) carries only ProductID. The hub is therefore anchored on ProductID so those relations can attach, and ProductNumber is kept as a descriptive attribute.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because ProductSubcategory references categories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because Product references subcategories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model shared by several products. Anchored on the ID because Product and the association tables reference models by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation, identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure, identified by a short code.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description held in a library, independent of any one product.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Photograph in the product photo library.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (document or folder) in the hierarchical controlled document library.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory location. Anchored on the ID because inventory and routing reference locations by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason. Anchored on the ID because WorkOrder references scrap reasons by ID.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live and the archive store so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer review of a product.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_line
hubs.description: A purchase order line, identified by its purchase order together with its line number. Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the line.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: Shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) used for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders carry, so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in the satellite.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Which addresses a party uses and in what capacity; party+address+type is unique.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + AddressID + AddressTypeID

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisation (business entity) to the person acting as its contact, in a contact role; organisation+person+role is unique.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID (organisation) + PersonID + ContactTypeID

links.name: link_business_entity_phone_number_type
links.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + PhoneNumberTypeID (phone number as child key)

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits (country derived via state).

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and a shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. An effectivity satellite tracks the start and end dates for each employee.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID (assignment starting at StartDate)

links.name: link_business_entity_job_candidate
links.description: Links a candidate record to the employee hired from it. If this link exists, the applicant was hired.
links.unit_of_work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID

links.name: link_product_product_subcategory
links.description: A product belongs to at most one subcategory. The link is optional.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_product_category
links.description: A subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_product_model
links.description: A product belongs to at most one product model.

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_assembly_component
links.description: Bill of materials. An assembly product is made of a component product, with the component quantity expressed in a unit of measure. The structure is recursive.
links.unit_of_work: ProductAssemblyID + ComponentID (+ UnitMeasureCode)

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture
links.description: A product model described by a product description in a specific culture.
links.unit_of_work: ProductModelID + ProductDescriptionID + CultureID

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Many-to-many association of illustrations with product models.

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with photographs.

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with documents.

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner. The owner is an employee held in the existing HR hub (Document.Owner maps to BusinessEntityID).

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory: a product held at a location (many-to-many).

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: The product a work order manufactures.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order. The link is optional.

links.name: link_work_order_product_location
links.description: Work order routing: operations of a work order for a product, performed at a manufacturing location.
links.unit_of_work: WorkOrderID + ProductID + LocationID (operation sequence as dependent key)

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: The product moved by an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: The product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Supply relationship between a product and the vendor (business entity) that supplies it, together with the unit of measure the product is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (+ UnitMeasureCode) from ProductVendor

links.name: link_purchase_order_vendor_employee_ship_method
links.description: Purchase order header relationship: each order is placed with one vendor, created by one employee and shipped by one shipping method. Vendor and employee are both business entities, so each takes part under its own role.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + VendorID + EmployeeID + ShipMethodID from PurchaseOrderHeader

links.name: link_purchase_order_line_product
links.description: Places each purchase order line in its order and ties it to the one product it refers to.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID + ProductID from PurchaseOrderDetail

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical replication metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person type and name details with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary name/contact PII; carries the Person ModifiedDate once.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_marketing_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion consent level, historised for audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Consent is a distinct classification with its own audit need and rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact info and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive data classification restricted separately from name reporting.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are excluded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded from the warehouse.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: All email addresses of a person, numbered within the person, historised.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source at finer grain, several concurrent rows per person.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_phones
satellites.description: Telephone numbers of a person per phone type, historised.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of party-address relationships.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of contact relationships.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details, historised.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of the address.
satellites.split_rationale: Distinct data type (spatial) and sensitive classification.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State/province code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of the state/province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory assignment changes at a different rate and needs separate history tracking.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Non-sensitive employee details: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active status and network login. Changes are kept so values that the source overwrites still have a history.
satellites.split_rationale: General employment attributes that change slowly and are not restricted; holds the single ModifiedDate audit column for Employee.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Personal and sensitive employee attributes, with access limited to authorised HR users.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII) so that access can be restricted.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Point-in-time readings of vacation and sick-leave balances. Keeping each change shows how balances move over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by rate of change: balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the organisational hierarchy. History is captured as changes occur.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position is its own concern and changes on a different schedule from other attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_pay_history
satellites.description: Pay rate history. RateChangeDate (the effective date) separates the concurrent records.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from a separate source table at a finer grain (one row per rate change). EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. An assignment with no end date is the current one.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_audit
satellites.description: When each assignment record was last updated, used to judge how current it is.
satellites.split_rationale: The audit timestamp is kept apart from the effectivity dates.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-change date. History is kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift name and start/end times. History is kept because definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé, stored as a structured document. It is non-employee personal data, subject to its own retention rules.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes, including the natural product number.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive classification of the product.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial figures that change at a different rate from descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy
satellites.description: Inventory planning parameters.
satellites.split_rationale: Supply-chain planning parameters, maintained separately.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events with their own rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per cost period).

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per price period).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_content
satellites.description: Structured catalogue description and manufacturing instructions.
satellites.split_rationale: Large structured-document content, split from the lightweight descriptive data by data type.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Free-text marketing description.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Photo file names for the thumbnail and large versions.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_images
satellites.description: Binary images for the thumbnail and large versions.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary content split out by data type; whether it is needed is still to be agreed.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_diagram
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata: title, folder flag, hierarchy level, revision, engineering change number, approval status, file name and type, and summary. Full binary content is excluded until confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location name, standard hourly cost rate and capacity in hours.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason failure description.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_product_location_operation
satellites.description: Operation details for each operation sequence: scheduled and actual dates, resource hours and costs.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin. Captured over time to build inventory history.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Flag marking the principal image of the product.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_effectivity
satellites.description: Period during which a component is used in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_details
satellites.description: Bill of materials level and component quantity per assembly.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details. The order reference is kept as an identifier and is read together with the transaction type.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: live store.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive
satellites.description: Archived transaction details, which together with the live store form one continuous history.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: Split out as personal data under data protection classification.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identification and descriptive details: account number, company name and the optional purchasing web service address.
satellites.split_rationale: Identifying details that rarely change, kept apart from the commercial status codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor credit rating, preferred status and active flag, with history kept so the vendor's state at order time can be reconstructed.
satellites.split_rationale: Coded status attributes that change faster and whose history is explicitly required. Holds the single ModifiedDate for the Vendor source.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Standing commercial terms agreed for a product from a vendor: lead time, standard price and order quantity bounds. History is kept for trend analysis.
satellites.split_rationale: Agreed terms that change slowly. Holds the single ModifiedDate for ProductVendor.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_receipt
satellites.description: Running purchasing figures for the supply relationship: last receipt cost and date, and quantity currently on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Running values that change with each order or receipt, much faster than the agreed terms.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_status
satellites.description: Purchase order status and revision number, with history kept so status transitions and revisions can be traced.
satellites.split_rationale: Workflow attributes that change with each revision or status transition. Holds the single ModifiedDate for PurchaseOrderHeader.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_details
satellites.description: Purchase order dates and financial totals: order date, estimated ship date, subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Order dates and monetary totals, split from the workflow status attributes.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_details
satellites.description: Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total.
satellites.split_rationale: Terms fixed when the order is placed, which rarely change afterwards.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities per line. History is kept so the quantity received as at a date, and partial deliveries, are visible.
satellites.split_rationale: Receipt progression that changes with each delivery. Holds the single ModifiedDate for PurchaseOrderDetail.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_details
satellites.description: Shipping company name and agreed ship base and ship rate, with history kept so historical freight can be checked against the rates then in force. The rowguid replication identifier is left out.

evidence: Customer.AccountNumber is 'Unique number identifying the customer assigned by the accounting system', so it is an alternate key of the customer concept.
No existing hub models customers. The only account-number-like items in the vault are none, so there is nothing to match.
Customer.CustomerID is its own primary key ('Primary key.') and no existing hub has CustomerID as a business key.
Customer.PersonID and StoreID are only foreign keys to Person/Store. They show that a customer references a business entity, not that it is one.
Store.BusinessEntityID is the same identifier as hub_business_entity's business key, BusinessEntityID. The vault already feeds Person, Employee and Vendor into that hub on the same key.
Customer.StoreID is documented as 'Foreign key to Store.BusinessEntityID', which treats the store as a business entity.

The Store.BusinessEntityID comment says 'Foreign key to Customer.BusinessEntityID', but Customer has no such column. It does not name BusinessEntity explicitly, so confidence is moderate and a reviewer should check.
SalesOrderNumber is a computed identifier ('Unique sales order identification number') for the sales order, which is a customer-side order.
The vault's only order hub is hub_purchase_order (PurchaseOrderID, from PurchaseOrderHeader), a vendor-side purchase order. It has a different key and a different concept.
SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderID is the primary key of customer sales orders.
The existing hub_purchase_order is keyed on PurchaseOrderID and fed by PurchaseOrderHeader (vendor purchasing). A different identifier and a different business process.
The comment reads 'Customer purchase order number reference'. It is a customer-supplied reference on a sales order.
hub_purchase_order holds the company's own vendor purchase orders keyed by PurchaseOrderID. No cross-reference or documentation says the two populations overlap.
The shared 'purchase order' name is only a name-level hint, so no merge. It is unclear whether this should be its own hub or just an attribute.
SalesOrderDetail has its own key (SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID). The existing hub_purchase_order_line comes from PurchaseOrderDetail, a vendor-side purchase order line.
The two lines are different business keys and different processes.
SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID is documented as 'Foreign key to Employee.BusinessEntityID'.
Employee already feeds hub_business_entity, so this is the same key population.
SalesTerritory.TerritoryID is a primary key. No existing hub has a territory key.
hub_country_region and hub_state_province are related geography but are keyed differently (CountryRegionCode, StateProvinceID).
Name is a description of the sales territory ('Sales territory description'), so it is an attribute or alternate key of the new territory concept. It is not a separate existing concept.
No existing hub models sales territories.
CreditCard.CreditCardID is a primary key. Nothing in the vault models payment cards.
CardNumber is an alternate identifier of the credit card concept, which has no existing construct in the vault.
It belongs with the new credit card concept.
Currency.CurrencyCode is the ISO currency code primary key. No existing hub models currencies.
hub_country_region is keyed on CountryRegionCode, a different ISO code. CountryRegionCurrency only links the two.
CurrencyRate.CurrencyRateID is a primary key. The vault has no exchange-rate construct.
This is the natural composite key of the same currency rate entity as CurrencyRateID.
No existing construct models exchange rates.
SalesReason.SalesReasonID is a primary key. No existing hub models sales reasons.
hub_scrap_reason is a manufacturing concept with a different key.
SpecialOffer.SpecialOfferID is a primary key. No existing hub models promotions or discounts.
ShoppingCartItem.ShoppingCartItemID is a primary key. No existing cart construct.
ShoppingCartItem.ShoppingCartID is an nvarchar(50) cart identification number that groups items. No table of its own is given.
No existing hub models shopping carts.
SalesTaxRate.SalesTaxRateID is a primary key. No existing tax-rate hub.
The StateProvinceID on it is only a foreign key to hub_state_province.
PersonCreditCard.BusinessEntityID is documented as 'Foreign key to Person.BusinessEntityID'.
Customer.PersonID is likewise documented as 'Foreign key to Person.BusinessEntityID'.
The vault's hub_business_entity is already fed by Person on BusinessEntityID.

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify every customer by the customer account number assigned by the accounting system, which uniquely identifies the customer.
The business must be able to distinguish an individual-person customer from a store customer, because the two are served, priced and reported on differently.
For an individual customer, the business must retain the reference to the person who is the customer.
For a store customer, the business must retain the reference to the store.
The business must know the sales territory in which each customer is located.
The business must know when a customer's record was last changed in the operating system, so that reporting can be reconciled against the source.
The business must be able to report the customer base by territory.
The business must be able to report the customer base by customer kind (individual vs. store).
The business must be able to identify each store by its business entity reference.
The business must record the store name of each store.
The business must know which sales representative is assigned to each store, since reseller relationships are managed by a named individual.
The business must retain the store demographics captured for each store, described as covering the number of employees, annual sales and store type.
The business must be able to segment reseller performance by store demographic characteristics such as store size or store type.
The business must identify every sales order by its sales order number, a unique sales order identification number.
The business must know which customer placed each order.
The business must know whether an order was placed online by the customer or entered by a sales representative, since this distinguishes the two sales channels.
For orders that were not placed online, the business must know which sales representative created the order.
The business must know the territory in which each sale was made, recorded on the order itself.
The order's territory is held separately from the customer's territory and the representative's current territory, and reporting must be explicit about which territory is meant.
The business must track the date each order was created.
The business must track the date each order is due to the customer.
The business must track the date each order was shipped.
The business must track the current status of an order using the operational status values: in process, approved, backordered, rejected, shipped, cancelled.
The business must be able to measure order fulfilment performance, i.e. whether orders shipped on or before their due date.
The business must retain the customer's own purchase order number where the customer supplied one, so that reseller enquiries can be answered in the customer's own terms.
The business must retain the financial accounting number reference carried on the order, to allow reconciliation with finance.
The business must know the billing address used for each order.
The business must know the shipping address used for each order, as a piece of information separate from the billing address.
The business must know the shipping method chosen for each order.
The business must retain sales representative comments recorded against an order, as context for enquiries and disputes.
The business must be able to report order counts and values by channel.
requirements.obj: order counts and values by channel

requirements.text: The business must be able to report order counts and values by territory.
requirements.obj: order counts and values by territory

requirements.text: The business must be able to report order counts and values by representative.
requirements.obj: order counts and values by representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to report order counts and values by customer.
requirements.obj: order counts and values by customer

requirements.text: The business must be able to report order counts and values by period.
requirements.obj: order counts and values by period

requirements.text: The business must track the revision number of an order, an incremental number tracking changes to the order over time, so it can tell that an order has been amended and how many times.
The business must record the order subtotal, described as the sum of the line totals for the order.
The business must record the tax amount charged on the order.
The business must record the freight (shipping cost) charged on the order.
The business must record the total due from the customer, described as subtotal plus tax plus freight.
The business must be able to analyse revenue with tax and freight separated from product revenue, since these are managed by different parts of the business.
requirements.obj: revenue separating tax and freight from product revenue

requirements.text: The business must know which credit card was used to pay for an order, where a card was used.
The business must retain the credit card approval code provided by the card company, for payment reconciliation and dispute handling.
The business must be able to report the share of orders paid by card versus those with no card recorded.
requirements.obj: share of orders paid by card

requirements.text: The business must know which currency exchange rate was applied to each order, where the order was not in the company's base currency.
requirements.obj: currency exchange rate applied to order

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales in the transaction currency.
The business must be able to report sales converted to a reporting currency, using the rate that applied to the order.
The business must identify each order line within its order, using one incremental unique number per product sold.
The business must know which product was sold on each order line.
The business must know the quantity ordered per product on each line.
The business must know the unit selling price of the product on each line.
The business must know the discount amount applied to each line.
The business must know the line total, described as unit price × (1 − discount) × quantity.
The business must know which special offer (promotional code) applied to each line, so that promotional effectiveness can be measured.
The business must retain the shipment tracking number supplied by the shipper for each line, because lines of one order may ship separately.
requirements.obj: carrier tracking number of order line

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse sales by product, by quantity, by realised price and by discount level.
requirements.obj: sales by product, quantity, realised price and discount level

requirements.text: The business must be able to distinguish list-price revenue from discount given away, at line level.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales reasons, each with a description.
Each sales reason must belong to a reason category.
The business must know which sales reasons were recorded against each order.
An order may have several sales reasons, and a sales reason may apply to many orders.
The business must be able to report order volume and value by sales reason and by reason category.
requirements.obj: order volume and value by sales reason and category

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the proportion of orders for which no sales reason was recorded, as a data-quality measure.
requirements.obj: proportion of orders without sales reason

requirements.text: The business must identify each sales representative by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference.
The business must know the territory a representative is currently assigned to.
The business must know each representative's projected yearly sales quota.
The business must know the bonus due to a representative if the quota is met.
The business must know the commission percentage a representative receives per sale.
The business must know each representative's year-to-date sales total and previous-year sales total as maintained by the operational system.
The business must be able to compare a representative's actual sales against quota and identify who is on track to earn the bonus.
The business must be able to report sales by representative over time, independently of the running totals held in the operational system.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales territories, each with a territory name.
The business must know the country or region each territory belongs to.
The business must know the geographic group a territory belongs to, so that results can be rolled up regionally.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date sales and previous-year sales.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date business costs and previous-year costs.
The business must be able to report territory contribution, i.e. sales against costs, for the current and previous year.
The business must be able to roll territory results up to geographic group and to country/region.
The business must maintain the register of credit cards used for payment, identified by the card record held in the operational system.
The business must know the card type (card name), the card number, and the expiry month and year of each credit card.
requirements.obj: credit card type, number and expiry

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales by card type.
Access to credit card numbers and expiry data, being sensitive personal and payment information, must be restricted.
The business must state whether the card number is needed at all in the warehouse or whether a masked or partial value is sufficient.
requirements.obj: need for full credit card number

requirements.text: The business must know which credit cards belong to which person.
A person may hold several credit cards, and a card may be associated with more than one person.
The business must be able to identify cards used on orders that are not registered to the ordering customer, as an input to fraud and data-quality review.
requirements.obj: cards used on orders not registered to the ordering customer

requirements.text: The business must retain shopping cart items, each identified within its shopping cart.
The business must know the shopping cart identifier for each cart item.
requirements.obj: shopping cart identifier of cart item

requirements.text: The business must know the product for each cart item.
The business must know the quantity ordered for each cart item.
The business must know the date and time each cart item was created.
requirements.obj: creation date and time of cart item

requirements.text: The business must be able to report which products are added to carts, and in what quantities.
requirements.obj: products added to carts and quantities

requirements.text: The business must be able to measure cart activity over time, using the creation date of cart items.
The business must maintain the catalogue of special offers, each with a discount description.
The business must know each special offer's discount percentage.
The business must know each special offer's discount type category.
requirements.obj: discount type category of special offer

requirements.text: The business must know the group the discount applies to, described for example as Reseller or Customer, so that promotions can be reported per channel.
The business must know each special offer's minimum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's maximum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's start date.
The business must know each special offer's end date, i.e. the end of the period during which it is valid.
The business must be able to determine which special offers were valid at any given date, including offers that have since expired, so that historical orders can be explained.
requirements.obj: special offers valid at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each special offer.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per special offer

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each offer type and category.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per offer type and category

requirements.text: The business must know which products each special offer applies to.
A special offer may cover many products, and a product may be covered by several special offers.
The business must be able to check that the offer recorded on an order line was applicable to the product on that line, as a data-quality and pricing-governance control.
requirements.obj: applicability of order line offer to product

requirements.text: The business must maintain the list of currencies, identified by their ISO currency code, with the currency name.
The business must be able to present currency names in reporting rather than raw codes.
The business must retain exchange rates as a time series, recording for each rate the date and time the rate was obtained.
requirements.obj: exchange rate time series with rate date and time

requirements.text: The business must record for each exchange rate the currency converted from and the currency converted to.
requirements.obj: from-currency and to-currency of exchange rate

requirements.text: The business must retain the average exchange rate for the day, as it serves a different reporting purpose than the end-of-day rate.
requirements.obj: average exchange rate for the day

requirements.text: The business must retain the final (end-of-day) exchange rate, as it serves a different reporting purpose than the average rate.

The business must be able to reproduce the exchange rate that was actually applied to a given order, not merely today's rate, so that historical reporting is stable and does not change when rates move.
The business must be able to report the same sales figures in more than one currency.
The business must state which of the two rates (average or end-of-day) is used for each report.
The business must be able to identify orders where no exchange rate was recorded and understand how those are to be treated (presumed base currency).
The business must know which currencies are used in which countries/regions.
A country/region may be associated with more than one currency, and a currency with more than one country/region.
The business must be able to check that sales in a given country/region were transacted in a currency valid for that country/region.
requirements.obj: validity of sales currency for country/region

requirements.text: The business must maintain the register of sales tax rates, each with a tax rate description.
The business must know the state, province or country/region each tax rate applies to.
The business must know the tax type for each rate, using the operational meanings: applied to retail transactions, applied to wholesale transactions, or applied to all sales.
The business must know the tax rate amount.
The business must be able to report tax collected by jurisdiction and by tax type.
requirements.obj: tax collected by jurisdiction and tax type

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the tax amount charged on an order with the tax rates applicable to the relevant jurisdiction, as a compliance check.
requirements.obj: order tax amount with applicable tax rates

requirements.text: A sales order is placed by exactly one customer, and a customer may place many orders over time.
A sales order is handled by at most one sales representative, orders placed online by the customer have no representative, and a representative handles many orders.
A sales order is made in one sales territory, and a territory carries many orders.
A sales order consists of one or more order lines, and each order line belongs to exactly one order.
An order line sells one product, and a product is sold on many order lines.
An order line may be sold under one special offer, and an offer is used on many order lines.
A sales order may cite several sales reasons, and a sales reason may be cited on many orders.
A sales order may be paid with one credit card, and a card may be used on many orders.
A credit card may be registered to one or more people, and a person may hold several cards.
A sales order may use one currency exchange rate, and a rate may apply to many orders.
requirements.obj: sales order and currency exchange rate

requirements.text: A customer is located in one sales territory, and a territory contains many customers.
A customer is either a person or a store.
A reseller store is served by one sales representative, and a representative serves many stores.
A sales representative is currently assigned to at most one territory.
A sales representative has worked a series of territories over time.
A sales territory belongs to one country/region and to one geographic group.
A special offer applies to one or more products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
A country/region may trade in several currencies, and a currency may be used in several countries/regions.
An exchange rate converts from one currency to another on a given day.
A sales tax rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type.
A shopping cart contains one or more cart items, each for one product.
There is no recorded link from a shopping cart to a customer or to an order.
A sales order carries a billing address and a shipping address, which may differ.
A sales order is shipped using one shipping method.
For the explicitly historical parts of this area, the business must be able to answer what was true at a past point in time, not only what is true now.
The business must retain the full history of sales quotas per sales representative, including the quota date and the quota amount in force from that date.
The business must be able to determine the quota that applied to a sales representative at any point in the past.
The business must be able to compare the quota that applied to a representative in a past period with the sales actually achieved in that period.
The business must be able to report how a representative's quota has moved over time.
The business must be able to report how often a representative's quota was revised.
The representative record also carries a single current quota figure alongside the dated quota history, and reporting must state which of the two it uses.
The current quota figure on the representative record and the dated quota history must be reconcilable.
The business must retain the history of which representative worked which territory, with the date the representative started work in the territory and the date they left.
A representative's territory assignment is open-ended while they are still working the territory, with no end date recorded.
The business must be able to identify the currently active territory assignment for each representative.
The business must be able to determine who was responsible for a territory on any given date.
Historical sales must be credited to the representative who actually held the territory at the time of the sale.
The business must be able to see the sequence of representatives who have held a territory and how long each held it.
requirements.obj: sequence and duration of territory holders

requirements.text: The representative record also carries the currently assigned territory alongside the dated assignment history, the same current-versus-historical duality as for the quota.
Where an order's territory differs from the representative's territory at the time of the order, the business must be able to see and explain that difference.
requirements.obj: order territory versus representative territory difference

requirements.text: Exchange rates are a daily time series, and the business needs the rate as at the relevant date.
Exchange rates must never be retrospectively overwritten in reporting.
Special offers have explicit start and end dates.
The business must be able to determine the special offers that were live at any date, including expired ones.
requirements.obj: special offers live at a date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see how descriptive information changes over time where it matters commercially, in particular a customer's territory, a store's assigned representative, a store's demographics, a special offer's discount percentage and a territory's group.
requirements.obj: changes in descriptive information over time

requirements.text: Every record in this area carries a last-modified date and time.
The business needs the last-modified date and time as the primary signal that something has changed.
The business needs the last-modified date and time as the basis for reconciling warehouse content with the operational system.

For all other entities in this area, the operational system holds only the current state, so history for those entities can only be built from the point the warehouse starts capturing it, and the business must accept this.
The business must decide for which current-state-only entities building history is worth doing.
requirements.obj: entities for which history is captured

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales value and volume by period, territory, geographic group, country/region, representative, customer, customer kind, product, channel, currency, special offer and sales reason.
The business must be able to compare actual sales against quota per representative and per period, including the bonus and commission implications.
The business must be able to report territory profitability using sales and cost figures at territory level.
The business must be able to measure discounting: total discount given, by offer, by product, by channel and by customer kind.
The business must be able to measure fulfilment: order-to-ship elapsed time, on-time performance against due date, and the distribution of order statuses.
The business must be able to measure channel mix, comparing online orders with representative-entered orders in volume and value.
The business must be able to report tax and freight separately from product revenue.
The business must be able to report sales in a single reporting currency across all territories, using the rate that applied to each order.
requirements.obj: sales in a single reporting currency

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse the reseller base by store demographics and by assigned representative.
The business must be able to analyse online cart activity by product and period, within the limits of the missing link between shopping cart and customer or order.

The business must be able to see, for each order, whether the key commercial attributes are present: customer, territory, representative (where not online), currency rate (where non-base currency) and payment reference.
requirements.obj: presence of key commercial attributes on orders

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that the order total agrees with the sum of its lines plus tax and freight, and to report where it does not.
The business must be able to check that line totals agree with quantity, unit price and discount as described by the source.
The business must be able to report orders that reference a special offer outside its validity period at the order date.
The business must be able to report customers that are neither a person nor a store, or that are both, once the open question on customer kind is resolved.
requirements.obj: customers that are neither or both person and store

requirements.text: The business must be able to report representatives with no territory on any given date.
The business must be able to report territories with no representative on any given date.

The business must be able to reconcile operationally maintained running totals (representative and territory year-to-date and last-year figures) against totals recalculated from orders, and to report material differences.
requirements.obj: running totals against recalculated order totals

requirements.text: Each entity in this area must have a named business owner accountable for its definitions and for resolving the clarifications in the document.
Business owners must be assigned before the warehouse is built.
Credit card data (card number, expiry, card type, holder association) is payment-sensitive, and its handling, retention and access rules must be defined before it is loaded.

Individual customers are natural persons, and personal-data handling rules, including retention limits and the treatment of deletion requests, must be defined for the customer information in this area.
Sales representative quota, bonus, commission and achievement figures are remuneration data about identifiable individuals and must be access-restricted to those with a legitimate need.
Store demographics are commercially sensitive information about reseller partners and must be treated as confidential.
The replication identifier carried by several records has no business meaning and is not required by the business, but may be retained as a technical trace of the source record.
Values computed by the operational system (order number, customer account number, line total, order subtotal and total due) are to be taken as given from the source rather than recalculated.
Values computed by the operational system must be checkable by the business.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-001 states every customer is identified by the account number assigned by the accounting system, which uniquely identifies the customer; REQ-051-3 says it is source-computed and taken as given. Business-recognised, unique and stable.
System-generated surrogate for the customer in the source; no requirement names it as the business identifier (REQ-001 prefers the account number), so it is a weak business key.
REQ-009 states each store is identified by its business entity reference; unique, non-null and used by the business.
REQ-014 states every sales order is identified by its sales order number, a unique identification number; REQ-051-3 says it is taken as given from the source.
System-generated surrogate for the order header and the parent reference of order lines (REQ-044-2). Not called out as the business identifier, so it is weak.
REQ-025 says this is the customer's own PO number, retained only where supplied. It is nullable and not unique across orders, so it is not a business key.

REQ-048 says each line is identified within its order by one incremental unique number per product sold. It is a business key only together with the parent sales order number (composite), as REQ-044-2 says each line belongs to exactly one order.
REQ-064 states each sales representative is identified by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference.
Requirements (REQ-072, REQ-018, REQ-005) refer to territories only by name and catalogue, with no explicit identifier. TerritoryID is the source identifier and the best listed candidate.
REQ-072 says the catalogue of territories carries a territory name that the business uses to recognise territories. Uniqueness and stability are not stated.
REQ-079 says cards are identified by the card record held in the operational system. This is the only identifier given. The card number (REQ-080) is sensitive (REQ-082, REQ-046-3) and so a poor key.
REQ-080 lists the card number as an attribute. It is payment-sensitive and access-restricted (REQ-082, REQ-083), and REQ-085 says a card may be shared by several people, so it is not a preferred key.
REQ-022-2 states currencies are identified by their ISO currency code; it is unique, stable and non-null.

System identifier for an exchange rate record. REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2 and REQ-059-2 imply the natural key is the rate date plus from-currency and to-currency, but that is not stated as unique, so this is a moderate fallback.
REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2 and REQ-059-2 describe a daily series of rates converting from one currency to another. The composite fits the business description, but the requirements do not say it is unique.
REQ-058 describes a catalogue of sales reasons, each with a description, but gives no explicit identifier. The source ID is the best listed candidate, though it is a system-generated code.
REQ-054 refers to the special offer as a promotional code applied on order lines (REQ-008-2, REQ-046-2). The source ID is the only identifier among the known columns and is not stated as unique.
REQ-001-2 says each cart item is identified within its shopping cart. ShoppingCartItemID, together with ShoppingCartID (REQ-002-2), is the available identifier.
REQ-002-2 and REQ-061-2 describe a shopping cart identifier that groups cart items. It is the only cart identifier available, and no link to a customer or order exists (REQ-062-2).

REQ-035-2 describes a register of tax rates with descriptions. REQ-060-2 implies the natural identity is state/province or country plus tax type, but it is not stated as unique, so the source ID is a fallback.
REQ-003 and REQ-084 refer to a person reference for individual customers and card holders (PersonCreditCard). No explicit person identifier is stated, so this is a tentative key.

hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, stores, persons). Persons share the same business entity number, so person data attaches here as satellites rather than a separate hub. Email addresses and credentials are keyed by the same number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Countries and regions identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: States and provinces identified by their own number.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units in which people work. Keyed on the stable DepartmentID because department names can change.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts. Keyed on the stable ShiftID because shift names and definitions can be adjusted.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates whose applications are held by HR.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product master. ProductNumber is the business-recognised natural key (REQ-002), but every dependent relation (inventory, work orders, BOM, cost/price history, transactions, reviews, photos, documents) carries only ProductID. The hub is therefore anchored on ProductID so those relations can attach, and ProductNumber is kept as a descriptive attribute.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because ProductSubcategory references categories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because Product references subcategories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model shared by several products. Anchored on the ID because Product and the association tables reference models by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation, identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure, identified by a short code.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description held in a library, independent of any one product.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Photograph in the product photo library.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (document or folder) in the hierarchical controlled document library.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory location. Anchored on the ID because inventory and routing reference locations by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason. Anchored on the ID because WorkOrder references scrap reasons by ID.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live and the archive store so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer review of a product.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_line
hubs.description: A purchase order line, identified by its purchase order together with its line number. Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the line.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: Shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) used for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders carry, so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in the satellite.

hubs.name: hub_customer
hubs.description: Customer, identified by the account number assigned by the accounting system (source-computed, taken as given).

hubs.name: hub_sales_order
hubs.description: Sales order, identified by its unique sales order number.

hubs.name: hub_sales_order_line
hubs.description: Sales order line, identified within its order by an incremental number per product sold.

hubs.name: hub_sales_territory
hubs.description: Sales territory catalogue entry.

hubs.name: hub_credit_card
hubs.description: Credit card register entry, identified by the card record held in the operational system.

hubs.name: hub_currency
hubs.description: Currency identified by its ISO currency code.

hubs.name: hub_currency_rate
hubs.description: Daily exchange rate converting from one currency to another on a given day.

hubs.name: hub_sales_reason
hubs.description: Sales reason catalogue entry.

hubs.name: hub_special_offer
hubs.description: Special offer (promotional code) catalogue entry.

hubs.name: hub_shopping_cart
hubs.description: Shopping cart grouping cart items; not linked to customer or order.

hubs.name: hub_sales_tax_rate
hubs.description: Sales tax rate register entry.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Which addresses a party uses and in what capacity; party+address+type is unique.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + AddressID + AddressTypeID

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisation (business entity) to the person acting as its contact, in a contact role; organisation+person+role is unique.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID (organisation) + PersonID + ContactTypeID

links.name: link_business_entity_phone_number_type
links.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + PhoneNumberTypeID (phone number as child key)

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits (country derived via state).

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and a shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. An effectivity satellite tracks the start and end dates for each employee.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID (assignment starting at StartDate)

links.name: link_business_entity_job_candidate
links.description: Links a candidate record to the employee hired from it. If this link exists, the applicant was hired.
links.unit_of_work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID

links.name: link_product_product_subcategory
links.description: A product belongs to at most one subcategory. The link is optional.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_product_category
links.description: A subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_product_model
links.description: A product belongs to at most one product model.

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_assembly_component
links.description: Bill of materials. An assembly product is made of a component product, with the component quantity expressed in a unit of measure. The structure is recursive.
links.unit_of_work: ProductAssemblyID + ComponentID (+ UnitMeasureCode)

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture
links.description: A product model described by a product description in a specific culture.
links.unit_of_work: ProductModelID + ProductDescriptionID + CultureID

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Many-to-many association of illustrations with product models.

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with photographs.

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with documents.

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner. The owner is an employee held in the existing HR hub (Document.Owner maps to BusinessEntityID).

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory: a product held at a location (many-to-many).

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: The product a work order manufactures.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order. The link is optional.

links.name: link_work_order_product_location
links.description: Work order routing: operations of a work order for a product, performed at a manufacturing location.
links.unit_of_work: WorkOrderID + ProductID + LocationID (operation sequence as dependent key)

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: The product moved by an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: The product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Supply relationship between a product and the vendor (business entity) that supplies it, together with the unit of measure the product is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (+ UnitMeasureCode) from ProductVendor

links.name: link_purchase_order_vendor_employee_ship_method
links.description: Purchase order header relationship: each order is placed with one vendor, created by one employee and shipped by one shipping method. Vendor and employee are both business entities, so each takes part under its own role.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + VendorID + EmployeeID + ShipMethodID from PurchaseOrderHeader

links.name: link_purchase_order_line_product
links.description: Places each purchase order line in its order and ties it to the one product it refers to.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID + ProductID from PurchaseOrderDetail

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_customer_business_entity
links.description: Customer to the person (individual customer) or store (store customer) it represents.

links.name: link_customer_sales_territory
links.description: Sales territory in which the customer is located.

links.name: link_business_entity_store_sales_person
links.description: Sales representative assigned to a reseller store.

links.name: link_sales_order_customer
links.description: Customer who placed the sales order.

links.name: link_sales_order_sales_person
links.description: Sales representative who created the order (absent for online orders).

links.name: link_sales_order_sales_territory
links.description: Territory in which the sale was made, as recorded on the order (distinct from customer and representative territory).

links.name: link_sales_order_address
links.description: Billing and shipping addresses used for the order.

links.name: link_sales_order_ship_method
links.description: Shipping method chosen for the order.

links.name: link_sales_order_credit_card
links.description: Credit card used to pay for the order, where one was used.

links.name: link_sales_order_currency_rate
links.description: Exchange rate applied to the order, where not in base currency.

links.name: link_sales_order_line_product_special_offer
links.description: Order line within its order, selling one product under an optional special offer.
links.unit_of_work: SalesOrderID + SalesOrderDetailID with ProductID and SpecialOfferID of the line

links.name: link_sales_order_sales_reason
links.description: Sales reasons recorded against an order (many-to-many).

links.name: link_business_entity_sales_territory
links.description: Territory the sales representative is currently assigned to (from the representative record).

links.name: link_business_entity_sales_territory_assignment
links.description: Dated history of which representative worked which territory.

links.name: link_sales_territory_country_region
links.description: Country/region the territory belongs to.

links.name: link_business_entity_credit_card
links.description: Credit cards held by persons (many-to-many).

links.name: link_special_offer_product
links.description: Products each special offer applies to.

links.name: link_country_region_currency
links.description: Currencies used in each country/region.

links.name: link_currency_rate_currency
links.description: Currency converted from and currency converted to by an exchange rate.

links.name: link_sales_tax_rate_state_province
links.description: State/province jurisdiction the tax rate applies to.

links.name: link_shopping_cart_product
links.description: Cart items: products placed in a shopping cart.
links.unit_of_work: ShoppingCartID + ProductID of a cart item

links.name: link_sales_order_line_product
links.description: Declared foreign key SalesOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical replication metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person type and name details with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary name/contact PII; carries the Person ModifiedDate once.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_marketing_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion consent level, historised for audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Consent is a distinct classification with its own audit need and rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact info and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive data classification restricted separately from name reporting.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are excluded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded from the warehouse.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: All email addresses of a person, numbered within the person, historised.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source at finer grain, several concurrent rows per person.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_phones
satellites.description: Telephone numbers of a person per phone type, historised.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of party-address relationships.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of contact relationships.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details, historised.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of the address.
satellites.split_rationale: Distinct data type (spatial) and sensitive classification.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State/province code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of the state/province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory assignment changes at a different rate and needs separate history tracking.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Non-sensitive employee details: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active status and network login. Changes are kept so values that the source overwrites still have a history.
satellites.split_rationale: General employment attributes that change slowly and are not restricted; holds the single ModifiedDate audit column for Employee.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Personal and sensitive employee attributes, with access limited to authorised HR users.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII) so that access can be restricted.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Point-in-time readings of vacation and sick-leave balances. Keeping each change shows how balances move over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by rate of change: balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the organisational hierarchy. History is captured as changes occur.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position is its own concern and changes on a different schedule from other attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_pay_history
satellites.description: Pay rate history. RateChangeDate (the effective date) separates the concurrent records.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from a separate source table at a finer grain (one row per rate change). EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. An assignment with no end date is the current one.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_audit
satellites.description: When each assignment record was last updated, used to judge how current it is.
satellites.split_rationale: The audit timestamp is kept apart from the effectivity dates.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-change date. History is kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift name and start/end times. History is kept because definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé, stored as a structured document. It is non-employee personal data, subject to its own retention rules.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes, including the natural product number.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive classification of the product.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial figures that change at a different rate from descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy
satellites.description: Inventory planning parameters.
satellites.split_rationale: Supply-chain planning parameters, maintained separately.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events with their own rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per cost period).

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per price period).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_content
satellites.description: Structured catalogue description and manufacturing instructions.
satellites.split_rationale: Large structured-document content, split from the lightweight descriptive data by data type.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Free-text marketing description.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Photo file names for the thumbnail and large versions.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_images
satellites.description: Binary images for the thumbnail and large versions.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary content split out by data type; whether it is needed is still to be agreed.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_diagram
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata: title, folder flag, hierarchy level, revision, engineering change number, approval status, file name and type, and summary. Full binary content is excluded until confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location name, standard hourly cost rate and capacity in hours.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason failure description.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_product_location_operation
satellites.description: Operation details for each operation sequence: scheduled and actual dates, resource hours and costs.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin. Captured over time to build inventory history.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Flag marking the principal image of the product.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_effectivity
satellites.description: Period during which a component is used in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_details
satellites.description: Bill of materials level and component quantity per assembly.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details. The order reference is kept as an identifier and is read together with the transaction type.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: live store.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive
satellites.description: Archived transaction details, which together with the live store form one continuous history.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: Split out as personal data under data protection classification.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identification and descriptive details: account number, company name and the optional purchasing web service address.
satellites.split_rationale: Identifying details that rarely change, kept apart from the commercial status codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
